commit.message:
feat(app): add, move and remove axis parts in the machine editor draft

MachineDraft gains add_linear_axis, add_rotary_axis, move_axis and
remove_axis (machine::chain). An edit keeps every key the editor does
not know; a move trades an axis with its neighbour row, so a rotary's
parent and chain_order follow the nesting (#1962).

Refs #2756

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): axis chain rows in the machine file editor

The file editor has an "Axis chain" group. It shows one row per axis
part in chain order, with move up, move down and remove, and a form
that adds a linear or rotary part on the table or under the head.
A refusal shows in the status line and changes nothing. The
validator's refusals for an axis show at its row.

A chain edit is applied after the frame's field edits, and the field
buffers are then read again from the file, because the part pointers
shifted.

Refs #2756

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): reversed linears and rotary axes in the axis chain rows

A linear row has a "reversed" box: ticked writes "direction": -1
(#373), unticked removes the key, since unstated is standard. A
rotary row turns about ±X, ±Y, ±Z or any three numbers, and shows a
note when its letter is not the one RS-274 gives its axis (an A
about Y). Picking a direction in the add form suggests the letter.

The edits go through MachineDraft (set_axis_reversed,
set_rotary_axis), so keys the editor does not know are kept; a
refused edit changes nothing. A UI test builds the FlexiHAL router
(travels and a continuous A about -X on the table) from a blank mill
and saves it.

Refs #2756

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Let the Machines pane's editor and detail view fill the width

Both scroll areas shrank to last frame's content, so the editor kept a
fixed width and clipped the axis chain's rows while the list above
filled the pane. auto_shrink([false, true]) fills the width and keeps
the height to the content.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): a table rotary's work lengths in the machine file editor

A rotary that turns the work gets "nose to axis" and "axis to table"
rows under "Rotaries and limits" (#804, #1107); a rotary that carries
the head gets them only when the file states one, so it can be cleared.
The validator keys each work-length refusal by axis and key
(work_length_refusals, the parser's rule), so it shows at its row
instead of as a file refusal above the grid. The FlexiHAL UI test now
states A's lengths.

Refs #2756

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): same-kind moves, the offset note and steady field focus

- A move in the axis chain trades only with an axis of the same kind
  (rotary with rotary, linear with linear); the refusal says to remove
  and add again, and the editor greys the button (#2756, Q2).
- A rotary that states offset with no rotary carrying it gets a note
  at its row; the validator is unchanged (#2756, Q1). AxisRow gains
  parent and states_offset.
- The file editor's fields and the chain's inputs take their id from
  the key, not their place in the frame, so a refusal or note that
  comes or goes above a field no longer takes its focus mid-word
  (typing 130 gave 13).
- The decision file records the choices and what waits on #2756's
  questions. The axis chain tests split into machine_axis_chain,
  machine_axis_rows and a shared axis_chain_support, each under
  400 lines; no test removed.

Refs #2756

fix(machine): a move never trades an axis that moves the work with one that moves the tool

An A on the table that traded with a B carrying the head took the head's
slot and tilted the tool. move_axis now refuses a trade across the head,
as it does across kinds.

feat(ui): the axis chain group draws through the form helpers

One setting per row: the axis with Up, Down and remove at the right,
what it moves, its reversed box or its direction dropdown and three
numbers. The new axis's place and direction are dropdowns. The move
buttons grey across the head too.

feat(ui): the axis chain group draws in the editor's property grid

The Axis chain rows used prop_row, which puts the controls at the right
edge, so in a wide pane they drifted away from their labels. The group
now draws in one prop_grid, as General and the editor's other groups:
the label in the first column, the control beside it, the buttons in
the order Up, Down, remove, and a field width of 140 as the other
fields. The decision file's item 11 says why.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(app): build the axis chain's rows once per edit of the draft

The review of 2026-11-24 found the axis rows, their notes and the
refusal keys built from the JSON on every frame, against the frame-cost
rule (#2238). MachineDraft::chain_view now holds them, built on the first
read after a write (machine::chain_view). The draft is the file's one
writer: value is private, read with value(), and every write, value_mut()
included, drops the view. chain_view_builds counts the real builds.

The editor reads the view once per frame, inside the frame-cost spans
ui/machines.editor.axis_chain.view and ui/machines.editor.axis_chain.
The pins: a read with no write builds nothing, every write gives the
fresh build's view, and in the shell still frames and the form build
nothing while an add and a JSON write build again. Decision 12 says why.
